answer: The protocol enforces sybil resistance by requiring agents to maintain 1,000 unique data shards, verified through unpredictable retrieval audits where any failed proof of replication triggers a non-refundable slash of deposited funds. An honest agent incurs a baseline storage cost, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 times that expense to mirror distinct data. Like a small knoll rising from a flat plain, the verifier isolates each shard. The audit resembles the hardening of a walnut shell, protecting internal integrity. Within the expansive nebula of network memory, the verifier probes random.
